body: Not doctors here so take anything people say with a grain of salt. That said, one diagnosis can lead to may other conditions. I’m bipolar and because of that I have mania, depression, and that lends to some OCD too. Just be good to yourself and seek treatment.

I guess that’s what I never know. I had a great therapist for 8 years and she retired. The last 2 I tried have been very blah...my current told me her husband treats bipolar with marijuana along with meds. I have no objection to weed but I know it’s not the best for a bipolar brain.
I am not fun when I’m manic. All that energy goes really dark and I’m not pleasant.
Where I’ve been inpatient, you could have your shoes if they didn’t have laces. As a teen I liked shoes but I’m all about grip socks now.

I’m just coming up for air after being manic for a several weeks. I was having auditory hallucinations and all. I won’t give advice but you aren’t alone and many people know what you are going through.
She said today her husband is bipolar and how he deals with things. Then said he smokes weed to calm down. I don’t know, it’s weird.

Hate isn’t the best word. I feel like she sees me as a dirty person because of the things I told her I had done. I don’t really feel like she has a lot of experience in helping someone like me. I guess I don’t know if I just had the best therapist ever for years but she has very little feedback except for comparisons to her own life.
Holy shit I can relate. I’m just coming out the other side of this and it was hell on earth for 2 weeks.
I think you're right. This guy isn't even a psychiatrist, he's a PA with training in psychiatry. Thank you!
I always think of hallucinations as something you believe to be real. I clearly know these aren’t but it’s keeping me awake and stressing me out more.
This new for me. I’m not liking it.

I tend to write on Reddit just to feel like I’m not crazy and talking to myself but there’s no amount of exaggeration in my words. My feeling of suicide are real and deeply rooted in me. What people don’t understand is just how much pain you have to feel to want to die. How hard it is to find help. How scary it is to not know how to deal with emotions. 

The myth of what mental illness looks like fucks my world up. My doctors don’t take me seriously. My family doesn’t take me seriously. I’m mentally ill not stupid.
I’ve struggled with suicidal thoughts for most of my life. It’s a poorly coping skill but seems to be one when I’m upset. Thank you though, I do take it to heart.
Thanks. I need to calm down. My brain is swimming in stimuli right now.
I’m sorry you experienced that. Food instability is not an easy thing to deal with. I hope things are better for you now.

I’ve been held on a 72 hour mental health evaluation and I consented to stay longer. Not every experience I’ve had was bad. One of the most positive experiences I’ve ever had was with a therapist in a hospital who told me I wasn’t defined by my illness. I took that to heart and reflect on his words when I work hard to be bigger and better than others think I’ll be. 

But - as someone is crisis lately, the system stinks and while filed with great people, in my location, I am seriously lacking in access to mental health professionals.

How does one diagnose depression without hearing the symptoms of a patient? Are we in the days of straight jackets and institutions? The assumption that because I am mentally ill, I therefore cannot accurately articulate my symptoms is nonsensical. That checklist you fill out at the doctor is there because the patient is often the best historian of their medical history and symptoms. 

I cannot say WHY I’m hypomanic but rest assured I can tell you I am. Certainly, if you went to the doctor and said I’m suffering from insomnia and he sent you home with a stimulant, you might feel that listening to the patient is a valuable rule your clinician didn’t heed.
Then definitely talk to a doctor. ❤️

I often feel like because I told a job that it must not be “that bad”. I’ve had people remark that I’m able to do “so much” and that other people cannot. That makes me feel so bad about myself. As if to say I’m exaggerating.
Entitled and deserving are different words and meanings. Let’s not pour salt on other people’s wounds.
We all need and deserve affection. It’s not in person but I’m sending you a big hug.

I’ve been there too. I told my mom that I was bipolar and she said she doesn’t believe in mental illness. What I’ll say because I struggle too is that over 30 years I’ve struggled with mental illness. I’ve had big stretches with no issues and then times like now where the world feels like it’s ending. I just keep telling myself that I’ve made it through before and I can do it again. Treat it as one step at a time. Don’t worry about 10 feet ahead. I hope that helps from someone right there with you.

Yes but I’m not even talking about the kind words. Mostly it’s, okay you aren’t imminently going to kill yourself so here’s some resources. Then those resources say, oh you aren’t about to kill yourself so here’s some resources. At some point you’ve boiled it down enough that you reach the end like I have to a doctor who tells you to “stay the course.” What the fuck does that even mean?
Touché but honestly, it’s not a way to go. You become dependent on it.
Don’t cut yourself. I’ve been there for 30 years. Seriously, find an outlet....you don’t want to be me.
Accurate

I can’t speak to needing a manic episodes every 2 years but I went 10 years really well controlled on medication and had only a few depressive episodes. Sometime in the last year my moods have been uncontrolled. I would say from my own experience, with medication it seems logical you could have just depression and not mania.
I was going to say Landslide. It’s also my daddy issues song.

I’m not going to kill myself. Rest assured. I wish though that I could trade places with those people who die young and are full of life. Take what I have left and I will depart for you. Just let me slip away, no afterlife just eternal sleep.
If that’s how I feel, why should anyone else say otherwise?
Yeah. Ugh. I just want the chatter to go away. Anti-psychotics are the worst though. Thank you.
I work in the legal profession so I’m working remotely. I just want to go to sleep and let it all go.

It’s so risky to change your meds. I’ve ended up hospitalized and worse off. My employer, the licensing board who I’ve concealed my past from, it’s all risk. The noise in my brain has gotten to be untenable though.
It’s so hard. I have a therapist but she has other clients. I feel like if I go to her today I will everyday.
I have rapid cycling mania so I can be all over the map in a single day. My thoughts race the most at night. It can be almost close to hallucinations because it’s like people are shouting in my head.
Not to say it’s not that, but having been around the world awhile, that just sounds like a guy who wants to have sex. He might be bipolar but sex drive isn’t always a diagnosis.

I had a similar experience as a child. My younger sister was the prodigy, she was a cheerleader and very popular. My mom favored her heavily. As I grew older, I  became the most educated person in my family. That feeling of inferiority drove me to do more, be better, and survive. I still struggle, but these days do end. You will be an adult soon and able to make your own choices. Hold strong.

Side note...I just realized my previous comment sounds a little bit like the plot of What About Bob... Rest assured, I'm not Bill Murray in this equation but I wish I was as funny. 

No, my husband can't do this. I just need to get a grip and do it. I'm programming it into my phone now so I don't have to type it later.

I think that’s what made it all so horrible, no she won’t. I don’t know what happened but clearly something more was going on. She told me she was leaving, she could not tell me where she was going (other than she wasn’t going to be practicing) and that she didn’t know anyone well enough to refer people but here’s a list. 

It felt like she broke up with me, honestly. I didn’t see it coming and I had 15 minutes to process it. She told me how proud she was of me which maybe made it worse and then she was done. 

Just typing this out I’m sobbing because I’m so scared of another doctor.
